cyp2d6.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
cyp2d6.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
cyp2d6.def: The hepatic enzyme chiefly responsible for metabolising metoprolol. Reduced hepatic function — or a genetically slow-metabolizer phenotype — can prolong and intensify its effect unpredictably, which is the pharmacologic reason to favour esmolol when the course needs to stay reversible.

cyp2d6.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
cyp2d6.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
cyp2d6.def: The hepatic enzyme that activates codeine to morphine and metabolises oxycodone and tramadol; genetic variability in its activity produces poor, normal, or ultra-rapid metabolisers, with correspondingly inadequate analgesia or toxicity risk.

ct angiography.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
ct angiography.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
ct angiography.def: A contrast-enhanced CT scan that outlines the inside of the vessel lumen — fast enough and detailed enough to be the first-line test for suspected dissection.

ct angiography.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ct angiography.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ct angiography.def: Contrast-enhanced CT imaging of the vasculature, used here to localise an ongoing lower GI bleeding source before an endoscopic or interventional-radiology procedure is chosen.

av block.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
av block.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
av block.def: Conduction delay or failure at or below the AV node. First-degree and Mobitz I block carry some safety margin; Mobitz II, 2:1, and third-degree block ("high-grade") are the ones that matter here — they leave no AV-nodal reserve to absorb a drug that slows conduction further, risking symptomatic bradycardia or complete heart block.

av block.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity
av block.subtitle: Phenotype-Guided Management
av block.def: Delayed or blocked electrical conduction between the atria and ventricles — a hallmark of cardiogenic-phenotype CCB toxicity from verapamil or diltiazem.

aki.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
aki.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
aki.def: A sudden drop in kidney function. Here, a reason to individualise rather than enforce the SBP <120 target by default, since the kidney may already be under-perfused.

aki.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
aki.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
aki.def: A sudden drop in kidney function. NSAIDs remove a compensatory renal-prostaglandin mechanism, so AKI (or a low eGFR, or hypovolaemia) is a reason to avoid them rather than merely dose-reduce.

rass.title: Butyrophenone Selection
rass.subtitle: Acute Agitation & Hyperactive Delirium
rass.def: A 10-point scale (−5, unarousable, to +4, combative) used to document and trend a patient's level of agitation or sedation at the bedside. Validated in adult ICU patients; used here to make "reassess every 10–15 min" an objective, reproducible check rather than a subjective impression.

rass.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
rass.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
rass.def: A validated scale used to grade a patient's level of sedation or agitation; used as the outcome measure in trials comparing ketamine with haloperidol for acute agitation.

rass.title: Haloperidol Adjunct Selection
rass.subtitle: Midazolam vs Ketamine in Hyperactive Delirium with Severe Agitation
rass.def: A validated 10-point scale (−5 to +4) used in several of this review's included trials to grade agitation severity and define “adequate sedation” as a target score (e.g. RASS ≤ −1).

qtc.title: Butyrophenone Selection
qtc.subtitle: Acute Agitation & Hyperactive Delirium
qtc.def: The QT interval (time from the start of ventricular depolarisation to the end of repolarisation) adjusted for heart rate, since the raw QT shortens and lengthens with heart rate on its own. A prolonged QTc is the electrophysiological substrate for torsades de pointes.

qtc.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
qtc.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
qtc.def: The corrected QT interval on an ECG; this algorithm flags both tramadol and the antiemetics used for opioid-induced nausea (ondansetron, haloperidol) as QTc-prolonging.

egfr.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
egfr.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
egfr.def: A calculated estimate of kidney filtering capacity (mL/min/1.73 m²). Below 30 is an absolute NSAID contraindication here; 30–59 is treated as a high-risk feature requiring caution rather than avoidance.

egfr.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
egfr.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
egfr.def: The lab-estimated kidney-function value this algorithm uses repeatedly (most often the <30 mL/min threshold) to decide which opioids, NSAIDs, or adjuvants are safe to use or must be avoided or dose-reduced.

ppi.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
ppi.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
ppi.def: An acid-suppressing drug added alongside an NSAID in patients with GI risk factors (prior ulcer, anticoagulant/antiplatelet use, age) to reduce the chance of NSAID-associated ulceration.

ppi.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ppi.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ppi.def: An acid-suppressing drug given at high dose after endoscopic haemostasis for upper GI bleeding, to create a less acidic environment that stabilises clot formation over the treated lesion.

ppi.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
ppi.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
ppi.def: Gastroprotective co-therapy this algorithm calls for alongside systemic NSAID use in older adults — conditional on identified GI risk in the figure's own wording, but stated as mandatory whenever a systemic NSAID cannot be avoided in the manuscript's own text.

mcid.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
mcid.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
mcid.def: The smallest change in a pain score a patient would perceive as meaningful. This page anchors it to roughly 10 mm on a 100 mm visual analogue scale — a slightly conservative rounding of Kelly's empirically measured ≈12 mm minimum clinically significant difference.

mcid.title: Lidocaine vs Prilocaine
mcid.subtitle: Local Anaesthesia for Laceration Repair
mcid.def: The smallest change in an outcome (here, roughly 1.3 points on a 0–10 pain scale, or a standardized effect size of about 0.5) that a patient would consider meaningful — used to judge whether a statistically real difference actually matters clinically.

mcid.title: Midazolam versus Clonazepam
mcid.subtitle: Seizures, Acute Agitation & Anxiety
mcid.def: The smallest size of effect, expressed here as Cohen's d, that this review treated as clinically meaningful rather than merely statistically detectable: below 0.2 is below the threshold, 0.2–0.49 small, 0.5–0.79 moderate, and 0.8 or more large.

mcid.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
mcid.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
mcid.def: The smallest difference that patients and clinicians would consider meaningful. This review prespecified an absolute standardised effect size (Cohen's d) of 0.20 as the MCID threshold for judging whether a statistically significant finding was also clinically important.

mcid.title: Haloperidol Adjunct Selection
mcid.subtitle: Midazolam vs Ketamine in Hyperactive Delirium with Severe Agitation
mcid.def: The smallest effect size judged clinically meaningful. This review set its MCID at Cohen's d ≥ 0.50, converting a hazard ratio to an approximate standardised mean difference where needed — the near-direct ketamine-vs-midazolam trial's effect (d ≈ 0.49) sits right at this boundary.

mcid.title: Selection of a Neuromuscular Blocking Agent
mcid.subtitle: Succinylcholine vs Rocuronium for Rapid Sequence Induction and Intubation
mcid.def: The smallest difference in an outcome that this review's authors judged a patient or clinician would consider meaningful — used throughout to distinguish a statistically significant finding from one large enough to actually change practice (for example, a consensus-defined 30-second threshold for onset time, or 10 minutes for delay to post-intubation sedation).

vas.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
vas.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
vas.def: A 100 mm line patients mark to rate pain intensity, from "no pain" to "worst pain imaginable". The standard continuous pain-intensity measure the between-drug effect sizes on this page are anchored to.

vas.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
vas.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
vas.def: A validated self-report pain scale named in the manuscript's own text and Key Practice Point 1, but omitted from the figure, which lists VRS instead.

nrs.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
nrs.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
nrs.def: An 11-point (0–10) verbal or written pain-intensity scale, used interchangeably with the VAS in some of the trials behind this page. A fall of ≥1.3 points is treated as equivalent to a ≥10 mm VAS fall.

nrs.title: Pharmacological Pain Management in Elderly Patients
nrs.subtitle: Stepwise Analgesic Decision Algorithm, Age 65+
nrs.def: A 0–10 (or here, 1–10) self-reported pain-intensity scale; this algorithm uses it to stratify patients into Mild (1–3), Moderate (4–6), and Severe (7–10) tiers at Step 3.

ufh.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ufh.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ufh.def: An injectable anticoagulant that potentiates antithrombin's inhibition of both thrombin and factor Xa. Fully neutralised by protamine sulfate, unlike LMWH.

ufh.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
ufh.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
ufh.def: An adjunctive anticoagulant option alongside fibrinolysis, used either instead of or historically before age- and renal-adjusted enoxaparin.

crrt.title: The Adult with Obesity
crrt.subtitle: In Emergency and Critical Care
crrt.def: Continuous (rather than intermittent) dialysis used in critically ill patients, typically dosed by a target effluent (filtered fluid) rate per kilogram per hour.

crrt.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity
crrt.subtitle: Phenotype-Guided Management
crrt.def: Continuous dialysis/filtration support, whose filters and circuits can be clogged or interfered with by the hypertriglyceridaemia that high-volume lipid emulsion therapy causes.

ards.title: The Adult with Obesity
ards.subtitle: In Emergency and Critical Care
ards.def: Severe, diffuse acute lung injury causing hypoxaemia. Low-tidal-volume, lung-protective ventilation principles apply with or without a formal ARDS diagnosis in patients with obesity.

ards.title: Blood Gas-Guided Assessment
ards.subtitle: Of the Chemical Warfare Agent Casualty
ards.def: Acute, diffuse lung inflammation causing severe hypoxaemia, graded by the Berlin definition using the PaO2/FiO2 ratio.

rsi.title: The Adult with Obesity
rsi.subtitle: In Emergency and Critical Care
rsi.def: A fast-onset induction and paralysis technique used when aspiration risk is high. The review specifically warns against under-dosing rocuronium for RSI by using a fixed adult dose.

rsi.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
rsi.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
rsi.def: Near-simultaneous administration of an induction agent and a paralytic to secure the airway quickly, minimising aspiration risk; ketamine's role as an RSI induction agent is substantially revised by the 2025 RSI Trial covered in this tool.

co-oximetry.title: Lidocaine vs Prilocaine
co-oximetry.subtitle: Local Anaesthesia for Laceration Repair
co-oximetry.def: Multi-wavelength blood-gas analysis that can distinguish methaemoglobin from normal oxyhaemoglobin, unlike standard two-wavelength pulse oximetry — the test that actually confirms methaemoglobinaemia.

co-oximetry.title: Blood Gas-Guided Assessment
co-oximetry.subtitle: Of the Chemical Warfare Agent Casualty
co-oximetry.def: Multi-wavelength oximetry (laboratory or pulse) that measures carboxyhaemoglobin and methaemoglobin in addition to oxyhaemoglobin — needed because standard two-wavelength pulse oximetry cannot detect these dyshaemoglobins.

va-ecmo.title: Reperfusion Therapy
va-ecmo.subtitle: In Acute Pulmonary Thromboembolism
va-ecmo.def: A form of mechanical circulatory support that can stabilise a failing right ventricle, buy time for clot resolution, or bridge a patient to surgical or catheter-based reperfusion in refractory shock or cardiac arrest.

va-ecmo.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity
va-ecmo.subtitle: Phenotype-Guided Management
va-ecmo.def: Mechanical circulatory support bridging a patient through refractory shock or cardiac arrest until the body clears the ingested drug; does not remove the drug itself.

esketamine.title: Ketamine in Head Injury
esketamine.subtitle: Safety Analysis & Complication Management
esketamine.def: The S(+)-enantiomer of ketamine, roughly twice as potent as the racemic mixture used elsewhere in this algorithm — doses are halved whenever esketamine is substituted — and associated with somewhat fewer cognitive disturbances on emergence.

esketamine.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
esketamine.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
esketamine.def: The more potent enantiomer of racemic ketamine, with roughly three-fold greater NMDA receptor affinity; licensed in several countries for treatment-resistant depression.

grade.title: Midazolam versus Clonazepam
grade.subtitle: Seizures, Acute Agitation & Anxiety
grade.def: A structured system for rating how much confidence to place in a body of evidence for a specific outcome — from high down to very low — based on risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias.

grade.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
grade.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
grade.full: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation
grade.def: The framework this review used to rate certainty of evidence for each outcome as High, Moderate, Low or Very low, downgrading for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or publication bias.

grade.title: Haloperidol Adjunct Selection
grade.subtitle: Midazolam vs Ketamine in Hyperactive Delirium with Severe Agitation
grade.full: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation
grade.def: The framework used to rate the certainty of evidence for each outcome in this review, from very low to high, based on risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias. No outcome in this review reached moderate or high certainty.

grade.title: Selection of a Neuromuscular Blocking Agent
grade.subtitle: Succinylcholine vs Rocuronium for Rapid Sequence Induction and Intubation
grade.full: Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation
grade.def: A structured framework for rating how much confidence to place in a body of evidence for a specific outcome (High/Moderate/Low/Very low), accounting for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias.

map.title: Vasopressor Agent Selection
map.subtitle: Aminergic Agents in Shock States
map.def: The average pressure driving blood flow through the arterial system over a full cardiac cycle (roughly diastolic pressure plus one-third of the pulse pressure). It is the vasopressor-titration target throughout this algorithm, with 65 mmHg as the initial threshold.

map.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Toxicity
map.subtitle: Phenotype-Guided Management
map.def: The average arterial pressure over a cardiac cycle, used here as the resuscitation target for vasopressor titration in vasoplegic-phenotype shock.

nmda.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
nmda.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
nmda.def: An excitatory glutamate receptor subtype; ketamine's primary action is non-competitive antagonism of this receptor at the phencyclidine binding site within its ion channel.

nmda.title: Haloperidol Adjunct Selection
nmda.subtitle: Midazolam vs Ketamine in Hyperactive Delirium with Severe Agitation
nmda.def: The receptor ketamine non-competitively blocks, producing dissociative sedation while relatively preserving airway reflexes and respiratory drive.

rob 2.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
rob 2.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
rob 2.full: revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials
rob 2.def: The five-domain tool (randomisation process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, outcome measurement, selection of the reported result) used to appraise this review's randomised evidence.

rob 2.title: Haloperidol Adjunct Selection
rob 2.subtitle: Midazolam vs Ketamine in Hyperactive Delirium with Severe Agitation
rob 2.def: The instrument used to assess risk of bias across five domains in each of this review's eight included randomised controlled trials, summarised in this review's Table 3.

rob 2.title: Selection of a Neuromuscular Blocking Agent
rob 2.subtitle: Succinylcholine vs Rocuronium for Rapid Sequence Induction and Intubation
rob 2.def: A structured tool for appraising bias in randomised trials across five domains — the randomisation process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, measurement of the outcome, and selection of the reported result. In this review, Domain 4 (measurement of the outcome) was the dominant source of downgrading, because succinylcholine's visible fasciculation can unblind the clinician grading intubating conditions.
